patients.label: 20-year-old asymptomatic woman, G1P0, with a second-trimester intramural ectopic pregnancy managed surgically

identity_evidence.quote: A 20-year-old asymptomatic female, G1P0, with a history of curettage

attribution_limitations: The discussion says the 17-week uterine size "probably resulted from uterine rupture, heavy bleeding and hypovolemic shock"; this is hedged speculation (likely meaning what could have resulted), while the case text and introduction state the uterus was not ruptured and the sac was excluded without life-threatening haemorrhage. It is not treated as a source conflict and the rupture, bleeding and shock are not recorded as facts.
The sentence giving the MRI uterine size ends in an unclear clause ("because of pieces of evidence") and does not say what the enlargement is attributed to.

The authors say the gestational sac was "excluded"; the extent of excision, histology of the specimen and the fate of the fetus are not stated. Cited published cases in the discussion belong to other patients and are not recorded.
Placenta previa is stated as an abdominal ultrasound finding and placenta implantation is hedged as "likely"; the source does not say how the two relate or confirm either at surgery.

The hysterectomy is an if-then option worded "subtotal hysterectomy or hysterectomy", which asserts neither; the source states hysteroplasty was performed and never states that any hysterectomy took place.

evidence.quote:
Figure 1.
Ultrasonography showedthe gestational sac (star) at a distance from the endometrial cavity (triangle), with a compressed myometrium (diamond) between the two of them. The compressed uterus cavity distal segments (arrows) showed a cambered thin line.

Figure 2.
T_(2) weighted coronal MRI image showed a foetus with clear organs and compressed lower uterine segment (white arrow).

Figure 3.
T_(2) weighted sagittal MRI image showed compressed lower uterine segment (white arrow).

Figure 4.
Linear hypointensity (white arrow) of the junction zone was observed between the gestational sac (triangle) and the uterine cavity (star) on T_(2) weighted image.

Figure 5.
Intramural ectopic gestational sac in the second trimester was successfully excluded without life-threatening haemorrhage.

Abdominal ultrasound showed a clear gestational sac, a fetus with heartbeat and placenta previa, with the sac at a distance from the uterine cavity and compressed myometrium between them.
